blindSummary:
This state/province holds the most active sub-national anti-discrimination ordinance cluster outside the country's capital region. A constituent city signed the implementing rules of its anti-discrimination ordinance in July 2024 in formal partnership with a regional LGBT federation and a UN development programme — an operational, not merely symbolic, protection framework. A municipality on the main island of this state/province approved a comprehensive anti-discrimination ordinance protecting people on SOGIE grounds by unanimous local-council vote in June 2025.

No killings, assaults, or institutional hostility incidents specific to trans visitors or residents were documented in this state/province within the 2024-2025 violence series or elsewhere in the dossier.

Net effect: above the country-wide average. A visitor to the main island's cities can file an anti-discrimination complaint under an operational ordinance — the practical equivalent of the capital region's protections without the accompanying violence signal. Compare another sibling region, which shows the opposite pattern: institutional hostility (a state university campus exclusion) without a compensating protective ordinance.
